There is a city named Ujjayinī, which possesses great moats and great halls;
it is like the great ocean and the great mountain.
The great earth itself was like a girdle (mekhalā),
where they beheld palaces built in continuous rows, made of gold and silver.
The people of Naga do not long for the peaks of Mount Meru or Kailāsa; rather, they take delight in the lute-like strings of the Vedas. //1.2//

Enough with describing that city,

Having abandoned [the world for] the city of Śiva, the Gaṇas departed. In that [city] sat Mahāsena;
Mahāsena was the lord of the earth.
Of him who, like the Lord of Śrī, long protected [the earth] while possessing sixteen thousand goddesses; //1.5//
